_about: Chapter T (Traverse) of the suite results document, the v5 prose round (2026-10-15): the prose data of DESIGN-DOC.md section 5 in R.json's shape, written for the union of the v4 mapping (doc/units/suite_v4.json: 15 families, 15 units) and the v5 mapping (doc/units/suite_v5.json: 16 families, 16 units; T-longwalk is v5-only, and T-attempts-0003, T-caps-0002..0004, T-quorum-0002 and T-seeds-0002 join their families' units). `summary` (what held, and the timing in one paragraph) and `coverage_gap` (which claim remains unsupported) print first on the chapter page, before and after the summary block; `intro` is the shortened /traverse background; `families` keys on the family id with a title, one paragraph and a `claim` (over `claim_members` when the claim rests on some members only); `units` keys on the unit id with its one-line property (a string or {property, note}); `mcp_notes.units` the one line under a unit whose MCP column is wholly not exercised; `coverage_gap_families` the families whose footnoted tests the gap discusses itself. Inline markup: `code` and *emphasis*. EVERY FIGURE OF THE RUN IS A PLACEHOLDER and every sentence whose truth depends on the run is a conditional `[[flag ? when true | when false]]` on facts.chapter_facts / family_facts / scenario_facts (the vocabulary of doc/facts.py; the facts this chapter needs beyond R's are listed in NEEDED-FACTS.md: `manifest_version`, the time-cut counts and texts, `x[sid][arm][time_limited]` and `x[sid][arm][checks][name]`). A sentence that holds in one manifest only is a branch of `[[manifest_version = 5 ? ... | ...]]`, never a reference to a scenario or family the other mapping lacks (an unresolved field prints as such). The literal numbers are the constants of the SPEC, of the manifests and of the service, each under `_assumes` with its source. Every claim follows SPEC-labeled-traversal-core.md sections 5 to 7 and 10.3, areas.py gen_T / _t_coverage / _t_gate_coverage, manifest_lib.py (the presets, traverse_by_design, mcp_traverse), checks.py and service_by_design.json. The readability review's chapter comments (2026-10-16, READ-101 and READ-110 to READ-117; lane RT): a `purpose` paragraph (support for a supplied sequence against extension of a supplied seed; the witness kind of evidence) and `evidence_map` true (the families' claims as a table after the headline, sections.claims_map); the conclusion names the three levels of an agreement; the Background keeps the server's coverage certificate, the test's minimum and the witness check apart, states what a pass proves with the T-end example and the recorded pass of T-walk-0001, explains the time budget as a timeline and what budget_respected certifies, and contrasts /resolve's deadline; T-budget explains the 1 ms pass from the recorded deadline details; T-attempts is written as a lifecycle with the inconclusive repeat explained; T-graphlet claims a serialisation witness, not equivalence with the full detail; T-walk and T-exhaustive name their witness; every unit carries a reader-level `question`; the family inventories are ids with a pointer to the exception index (`footnoted_ids`, `footnoted_elsewhere_ids`); and the prose says access path for a route to the host and traversal arm (direction) for a side of a walk, never a bare arm (READ-008 / READ-112).

intro: POST /traverse extends a seed through the graph under labels (SPEC-labeled-traversal-core sections 5 to 7). A seed is a sequence of at least k bases every k-mer of which is in the graph, with explicit labels (each must support every seed k-mer, else it is dropped as `seed_unsupported`; a seed with none left is refused) or without any, in which case the host derives the permitted set from the seed: the labels that carry every one of its k-mers, of the kind `labels.seed_label_kind` names, by default a header (an accession.version) on this index (section 6.1). From each requested traversal arm, that is, direction (right: the successors of the last seed node; left: the predecessors of the first; both by default; a traversal arm is a direction of the walk, never one of the three access paths) the walker follows a successor only while some permitted label supports it (`labels.mode` constrain), tracking per label the loss of its switches (none under the default `change_cost` forbid), splitting where labels diverge, merging routes that reconverge at the same depth, and ending a path with a stated reason: a label end (`label_lost`, `branch`, `below_min_labels`), a structural end (`dead_end`, `edge_reuse`, `rejoined_seed`), the radius `max_extension_bp`, or a resource reason when a cap or a budget stopped it (section 6.7). Annotate mode follows every structural successor and records the labels instead of filtering by them; the exhaustive preset forbids every pruning and answers a trie (section 6.9); trace support follows one indexed occurrence by consecutive coordinates (section 6.3). What a route establishes: under a taxid column the walker follows a successor while some record of the column supports it, so consecutive steps of one route may be supported by different records of the taxon; under a header label the successors are the record's own k-mers, and with trace support also at consecutive coordinates, the only mode that follows one indexed occurrence contiguously. A route is therefore label support along the way (I.1's result units), read as such by the checks; it is not by itself an observed contiguous sequence of any record other than the source the witness check compares it with.

Every answer certifies what it covers (section 7.0): per seed `outcome.walks` is complete, partial (a stated limit: a truncated or pruned traversal arm, a cut carrier set) or failed (no traversal: the set could not be derived, or a request budget did not hold the seed); per traversal arm `status` complete, truncated or pruned with `cap_trigger` naming the cap, `complete_to_bp` the depth to which every admissible walk is present (section 6.10), and `limitations` naming the knob to turn; a request budget's stop adds a `resource_stop` (time, memory or work) with the request's value. Three statements are kept apart throughout this chapter: the server's coverage certificate (`outcome.walks` and `complete_to_bp`: what the answer claims to hold), the test's expected minimum (how far the record's continuation must be followed, computed from the record), and the witness check itself (that some returned route spells that continuation). The scopes of section 6.8: `max_extension_bp` and `min_live_labels` per path, `max_steps`, `time_budget_ms`, `max_memory_mb` and `max_work_units` per seed, `max_live_paths`, `max_paths` and `max_output_bp` per traversal arm (direction). The time budget governs the walk of one seed, not the request: the host first prepares the seed (maps its k-mers, resolves or derives its labels and reads the roots' rows: the seed phase, which the budget does not govern), then walks level by level, reading the deadline on the seed's own clock at every checkpoint from depth 1 on (never at depth 0), and finally serialises the answer; a budget that has already passed when the walk begins stops it at the first depth-1 checkpoint, and a level at the radius is never stopped. `budget_respected` certifies that rule against the answer's own deadline record (that the stop came where the rule allows it), not that the client saw an answer within the budget: I.2's budget table gives the scope, appendix A's decision table the cases. A /resolve budget is another rule, one deadline on the whole request from the parsed body, a 503 past it (chapter R). Validation is strict (section 5): an unknown key, a wrong type or a value out of range is a 400 naming the field; a bound above the server's cap is lowered and echoed in `strategy.clamped` (section 10.3; `max_time_ms` 60,000 on staging), whereas more seeds than `max_seeds` (4 here) are refused. A request with `attempt_id` is an attempt: its answer states `usage` with the bound the server enforces on it (section 6.8), an id still retained is refused 409 as a duplicate, and a `not_after_ms` in the past is refused 409 as expired before anything runs (T-attempts shows the lifecycle).

Ground truth. The seeds are windows cut from the records of I.2, walked under the record's header, its taxid column or, for the derived families, no label. The property check `walk_in_record` asks that some root-to-leaf route of every requested traversal arm (direction) spells the record's own continuation of the seed (the segments concatenated, through any parent at a merge) for the whole minimum the builder computed from the record: on a whole record under its header exactly, as the first base where the record offers a second successor on either strand, the first reused edge, the record's end or the radius (manifest_lib.walk_expectations); otherwise the least of the radius, the record's end and the truth's flank, where a route may also end earlier at a stated branch or re-entry, since other records of a column, or other taxa, can branch where this record does not. What a pass proves: that one route per requested direction spells the record's continuation to the minimum. It is a witness test, not an enumeration of the routes the graph admits, so it says nothing about the answer's other routes beyond their label support (section 6.3), and a pass need not reach the numerical radius, since the minimum is the record's: a T-end seed 40 to 100 bp from its record's end passes at the record's end under a radius of 200 bp, and a header walk passes at the record's first branch. [[x[T-walk-0001][dl][pass] ? In this run the pass of T-walk-0001 on direct-local reads, in the check's own words: {x[T-walk-0001][dl][checks][walk_in_record][detail]}.]] A walk a stated resource limit stopped before the minimum is inconclusive, never a pass; a stated stop that cannot have happened fails. Every request sends the MCP preset's merged strategy with the scenario's overrides, so that the three access paths ask the same question: the walk preset (constrain mode, `max_label_branches` 2, 15,000 ms, 512 MB, 100,000,000 work units, 500,000 output bp per traversal arm, radius 5,000 bp), the trie preset (exhaustive, 30,000 ms, 1,000 live paths, 2,000 bp) or the trace preset (the walk preset with trace support and `on_reconverge` keep), with `output.detail` full (graphlet for T-graphlet). [[manifest_version = 5 ? Manifest v5 places a warm-up resolve (chapter R's R-warm) right before the walks whose rows are those of multi-copy k-mers (T-repeat), of a wide column (eco's column-kind derived walk) or of a seed in lambda's column (T-walk-0009), so that the target meets rows the host has just read; the document states the warm-up and its re-run beside the target's time and attributes nothing to it.]]

Via MCP a walk is the `traverse_fetch` tool: a preset (walk, trie or trace) with overrides of `bounds.*`, `direction`, `exhaustive`, `labels.max_labels_per_node` and `labels.seed_label_kind`; any other strategy key is refused by the tool naming it (the advanced strategy path, not enabled on this deployment) or has no argument, and the attempt fields, a graph field and a non-object body cannot be sent. The service validates in its own terms before the host: a budget above the preset's row (walk 15,000 ms, 512 MB, 100,000,000 units; trie 30,000 ms) and a bound above its own maxima (`max_live_paths` 1,000, `max_extension_bp` 10,000) are refused at submit, a seed shorter than k, a character outside ACGT and an empty label list are refused with its own text, identical seeds are merged onto the first, more seeds than the host's `max_seeds` are sent in batches, and the host's own 400 comes back relayed under `backend_rejected`. The service's answer is its graphlet export, from which the checks read the same walk as the direct access paths' full detail; it carries no label dictionary, so `label_dict_contains` is not exposed via MCP ([[manifest_version = 5 ? the manifest's property-level mark says so | in v4 the item reads not exposed and counts against a full check; v5 marks it at property level]]). Each MCP cell states its class in one line, and appendix B names every case with the service's code and text.

T-walk.title: walks
T-walk.prose: Windows of 31, 50, 100 and 200 bp cut from the records, walked right, left or both ways under one label: the record's header in two of every three scenarios, its taxid column in the third. The matrix groups the walks by direction and radius[[manifest_version = 5 ?: 100 and 1,000 bp; 300 bp for the three header walks whose 1,000 bp walk a cold first call left inconclusive in manifest v4 (T-walk-0004, -0014, -0022); and 10,000 bp for the two column walks of mge and pfa that end at stated branches within their first 4,000 bp (T-walk-0024, -0030), the four other 10,000 bp column walks of manifest v4 being T-longwalk's, each split into the gate's walk and a long twin |: 100, 1,000 and 10,000 bp, the longest on column labels, all under the walk preset's 15,000 ms]]. The property is `walk_in_record` (SPEC-labeled-traversal-core sections 6.3, 6.7 and 7.1): some root-to-leaf route of every requested traversal arm (direction) spells the record's own continuation of the seed for the whole minimum computed from the record (a witness: one route per direction, not every route of the answer, which the Background's 'what a pass proves' states), which on a header walk of a whole record is exact (the first base where the record offers a second successor on either strand, the first reused edge, the record's end, or the radius) and on a column walk is the radius unless a stated branch or re-entry ends the route earlier, since other records of the column can branch where this one does not; `traverse_seed_outcome` asks complete or partial, never failed. A walk a time stop cut before its minimum reads inconclusive, provided the stop can have happened (`budget_respected`, section 6.8). [[n_footnoted ? In this run {n_footnoted} test{n_footnoted:s} [[n_footnoted = 1 ? carries | carry]] a detail block after the table (an access path did not pass, or the paths answered differently: {footnoted_ids})[[n_time_cut_tests ?; {n_time_cut_tests} of the family's tests [[n_time_cut_tests = 1 ? was | were]] cut by a time stop before the minimum ({time_cut_ids})]]. | In this run every test passed on every access path, with the paths' answers alike.]]
T-walk.claim: a label-constrained walk follows the record to the minimum the record sets, or ends at a stated branch, in every direction and at every radius (one witness route per direction)

T-longwalk.title: long walks
T-longwalk.prose: The four column walks that no 15,000 ms call completed in manifests v3 and v4 (cje, scem, t4 and eco: every execution of theirs stopped by time), each split in two under the host's cap of 60,000 ms. T-derived.title: derived labels
T-derived.prose: A 100 bp window of a record with few relatives in RefSeq (buc, mge, mpn, ser, mja, sso) sent without labels, radius 1,000 bp: the host derives the permitted set from the seed, the labels that support every one of its k-mers, of the kind the index's default gives (header, since this index has a CoordToHeader), in ascending (column, sequence id) order and at most `labels.max_seed_labels` (the preset's default 1,000; SPEC-labeled-traversal-core section 6.1 step 4). T-end.title: record ends
T-end.prose: A 31 bp seed (one k-mer) 40 to 100 bp from a record end, walked toward the end under the record's header with a radius of 200 bp, on six records without terminal repeats (lam, t4, hsam, drem, dmem, scem; HSV-1's and HIV-1's ends repeat inside them). The record's label ends at its last k-mer, so the route following the record ends exactly at the record's end (`walk_end`: the route's length equals the distance to the end), with reason `label_lost` when the graph continues there through another record and `dead_end` when it has no successor (SPEC-labeled-traversal-core section 6.7); `walk_in_record` holds to the same end, and no route may run past it, the header being the only label. A traversal arm (direction) a stated resource limit stopped short of the end cannot show it and reads inconclusive. [[n_mcp_by_design ? Via MCP {n_mcp_by_design} of the {n_tests} pair{n_tests:s} stand by design: the request's budget is above the walk preset's row and the service refused it at submit ({mcp_refused_before_host_codes}; appendix B), so the record-end stop rests on the direct access paths there. | Via MCP no pair stands by design.]] In this run [[n_footnoted ? {n_footnoted:word} test{n_footnoted:s} [[n_footnoted = 1 ? carries | carry]] a detail block (an access path did not pass, or the paths answered differently): {footnoted_ids}; the exception index on the chapter page says what each exception means, the block holds the record | every test passed on every access path exercised, with the paths' answers alike]].

T-repeat.title: repeats
T-repeat.prose: A 100 bp seed inside a repeat its record holds in several copies (rRNA operons, IS elements: eco, bsu, sau, pae; the copies diverge within 950 bp on at least one side), walked [[manifest_version = 5 ? 400 | 1,000]] bp both ways under the record's header. T-labels.prose: Three questions on the label machinery. First, annotate mode (SPEC-labeled-traversal-core section 6.9) on a 100 bp seed of buc and of mge, radius 200 bp, `max_label_branches` unlimited: every structural successor is followed and the labels present are recorded, nothing is filtered, so a route following the record must be among the walks (`walk_in_record`, annotate scope). Third, `max_labels_per_node` 1 on a 100 bp seed under its header, radius 200 bp: the cap is echoed per traversal arm (`labels_per_node`, section 7.0) and the walk is unchanged; a list the cap cuts must be stated by a limitation naming the knob, but under a single header label [[x[T-labels-0007][dl][checks][labels_per_node][evidence] ? on direct-local the check recorded {x[T-labels-0007][dl][checks][labels_per_node][evidence]}, so nothing was cut | nothing was recorded as cut on direct-local]] and that statement is not exercised here. [[x[T-labels-0004][dl][pass] ? eco's header-kind walk passed on direct-local in {x[T-labels-0004][dl][wall]} ({x[T-labels-0004][dl][host_word]}) | [[x[T-labels-0004][dl][present] ? On direct-local eco's header-kind walk stands {x[T-labels-0004][dl][standing]} ({x[T-labels-0004][dl][host_word]}; `walk_in_record`: {x[T-labels-0004][dl][checks][walk_in_record][detail]}) | eco's header-kind walk was not exercised on direct-local]]]][[x[T-labels-0004][dr][pass] ?; on direct-remote it passed in {x[T-labels-0004][dr][wall]} ({x[T-labels-0004][dr][host_word]}). | [[x[T-labels-0004][dr][present] ?; on direct-remote it stands {x[T-labels-0004][dr][standing]} ({x[T-labels-0004][dr][host_word]}; `walk_in_record`: {x[T-labels-0004][dr][checks][walk_in_record][detail]}). |; it was not exercised on direct-remote.]]]] In this run [[n_footnoted ? {n_footnoted:word} test{n_footnoted:s} [[n_footnoted = 1 ? carries | carry]] a detail block (an access path did not pass, or the paths answered differently): {footnoted_ids}; the exception index on the chapter page says what each exception means, the block holds the record | every test passed on every access path exercised, with the paths' answers alike]].

T-exhaustive.title: exhaustive trie
T-exhaustive.prose: The trie preset (`exhaustive`: unlimited `max_label_branches`, `on_reconverge` keep, no quorum, no beam; `max_live_paths` 1,000, 30,000 ms; SPEC-labeled-traversal-core section 6.9) on a 60 bp seed of buc, mja and lam under the record's header, radius 100 bp. Under the preset nothing is pruned, so the result is the trie of every label-consistent walk to the radius or to the last complete level (section 6.10), and the record's own walk must be one of its leaves: `walk_in_record` (record scope, the exact minimum from the record). The trie is also the oracle the SPEC's verification contract compares a tuned walk against; this chapter asks only that the record's walk is in it, a witness leaf: that the trie holds every label-consistent walk is the server's own certificate (`complete_to_bp`), which no check here verifies independently, so one source-record route in it shows nothing of all-path completeness. In this run [[n_footnoted ? {n_footnoted:word} test{n_footnoted:s} [[n_footnoted = 1 ? carries | carry]] a detail block (an access path did not pass, or the paths answered differently): {footnoted_ids}; the exception index on the chapter page says what each exception means, the block holds the record | every test passed on every access path exercised, with the paths' answers alike]].
T-exhaustive.claim: the exhaustive trie holds the record's own walk as a leaf (a witness leaf; the trie's completeness is not checked independently)

T-coords.title: coordinates
T-coords.prose: Trace support with `output.coordinates` (SPEC-labeled-traversal-core section 7.1, feature level 6) on a 100 bp seed of eco, bsu and lam under the record's header, radius [[manifest_version = 5 ? 250 | 500]] bp, under the trace preset (the walk preset with `support` trace and `on_reconverge` keep: trace with merging is refused, section 13 item 9). With trace support a header label continues only while its coordinate continues by one (section 6.3), and the coordinates block reports where each run's sequence lies in the record: `trace_coordinates` asks that the seed's occurrence under the record's label is [start, start + length) and that each traversal arm's run of that label from the seed boundary lies adjacent to it, [end, end + L) on the right and [start - L, start) on the left; `walk_in_record` asks the route. These coordinates are positions in the record's bases (0-based, half-open), not the k-mer-start intervals of chapter R's runs. Not exercised via MCP: `output.coordinates` cannot be set through the tool, although the trace preset itself is accepted (see B)[[n_cold_dl ?; a test's first direct-local execution is host-cold for that reason (no MCP call reached the host before it; {n_cold_dl} host-cold direct-local execution{n_cold_dl:s} in this run)]]. In this run [[n_footnoted ? {n_footnoted:word} test{n_footnoted:s} [[n_footnoted = 1 ? carries | carry]] a detail block (an access path did not pass, or the paths answered differently): {footnoted_ids}; the exception index on the chapter page says what each exception means, the block holds the record | every test passed on both direct access paths, with their answers alike]].

T-budget.title: bounds
T-budget.prose: One bound set alone on a 100 bp seed under the record's header, radius 1,000 bp, each chosen to trip inside the walk: `time_budget_ms` 1 (a budget the manifest expects to pass during the seed phase, so that the first depth-1 checkpoint stops the walk: SPEC-labeled-traversal-core section 6.8), `max_memory_mb` 1 (a request budget that may fail the seed itself, section 5), `max_work_units` 300,000 ([[manifest_version = 5 ? on T-attempts-0002's eco window, whose seed phase both direct access paths of v4 charged 148,723 units, so that the budget holds the seed phase and stops the walk after a few tens of bases | on a seed whose seed phase alone may exceed it, which then fails the seed]]) and `max_steps` 5 (a cap: no `resource_stop`). The property is the stated stop of section 7.0 (`traverse_stop`): `outcome.walks` partial (failed allowed for the memory budget), a `resource_stop` of the budget's resource with the request's value, a requested traversal arm truncated with that cap trigger while every other traversal arm is so or complete, and a limitation naming the knob; the walk so far follows the record (`walk_in_record`, prefix only; a seed the budget failed is not walked and reads inconclusive). The 1 ms budget in plain terms: the host first prepares the seed (the seed phase, which the budget does not govern), then the walk reads the deadline at its first checkpoint, at depth 1, finds it passed and stops there with one base per direction; the client's wall holds the seed phase, that one level, the answer's serialisation and the transport, and via MCP the service's submit, queue and paging as well. `budget_respected` judges the time stop by the answer's own deadline record (a stop at depth 1 within the depth-0 levels' pieces; appendix A's decision table): its pass certifies that the walk stopped where the rule says, and nothing about the latency the client saw. A 1 ms budget is no 1 ms response, and this test makes no end-to-end latency claim; /resolve's deadline is another rule, one clock on the whole request from the parsed body (chapter R). [[x[T-budget-0001][dl][pass] ? In this run T-budget-0001 passed on direct-local in {x[T-budget-0001][dl][wall]} ({x[T-budget-0001][dl][host_word]}); the check's record of the stop: {x[T-budget-0001][dl][checks][budget_respected][detail]}; the walk so far: {x[T-budget-0001][dl][checks][walk_in_record][detail]}.]] In this run [[n_footnoted ? {n_footnoted:word} of the {n_tests:word} stops [[n_footnoted = 1 ? carries | carry]] a detail block (an access path did not pass, or the paths answered differently): {footnoted_ids}; the exception index on the chapter page says what each exception means | every stop passed on every access path exercised, with the paths' answers alike]].
T-budget.claim: each bound stops the walk with its own stated reason, and the walk so far follows the record

T-attempts.title: attempts
T-attempts.prose: An attempt is a request identity the server retains (SPEC-labeled-traversal-core section 5): a client that sends `attempt_id` can read afterwards what the request used, and is refused a second run of the same work while the id is retained. The suite exercises the lifecycle in three stages on a 100 bp seed of eco under its header, radius 200 bp. First, an already-expired request: `not_after_ms` 0, an instant long past, is refused 409 with state expired before anything runs or is registered, without `usage` (`answer_fields`). Second, a new retained identity: an `attempt_id` (unique per run and access path: the runner appends the run id and the access path, the manifest's `run_unique`) executes, and its 200 states `usage` with the bound the server enforces on it (section 6.8: seeds 1, the preset's 15,000 ms per seed, the allowance of 10,000 ms, and `walk_until_ms`). Third, the same identity again: [[manifest_version = 5 ? the same id sent again right after, while the server retains it (3,600 s), is refused 409 duplicate, carrying the attempt's state and usage and no response-level usage (sections 5 and 10.3). | the scenario's second repeat sends the same id and meets the retained duplicate's 409, which the manifest allows. That expected answer leaves the repeat inconclusive for the 200-only checks: the usage fields are checked on a 200 only, and the duplicate's 409 carries no response-level `usage`, so nothing of them can be read from it; the test's standing on a direct access path is the worse of its two repeats, although both answers are the ones the contract predicts, and the property table counts the attempt's properties as shown where repeat 0 passed them. [[x[T-attempts-0002][dl][present] ? In this run on direct-local T-attempts-0002 reads {x[T-attempts-0002][dl][phrase]}, so it stands {x[T-attempts-0002][dl][standing]} there.]]]] Both answers depend on the server's retention and on one server process (tag retention-dependent); nothing here is a replay of a cached result or a general retry guarantee. Not exercised via MCP: the attempt fields are the service's own, set by its worker, never by the caller (see B). In this run [[n_footnoted ? {n_footnoted:word} test{n_footnoted:s} [[n_footnoted = 1 ? carries | carry]] a detail block (an access path did not pass, or the paths answered differently): {footnoted_ids}; the exception index on the chapter page says what each exception means, the block holds the record | every test passed on both direct access paths, with their answers alike]].
T-attempts.claim: a start instant in the past is refused before any work, an attempt states its usage and bound, and a retained id is refused as a duplicate

T-edge.title: edge inputs
T-edge.prose: The edges of /traverse's validation, one input each, on a 100 bp window of E. coli under its header with a radius of 100 bp, unless the edge is the seed itself. Refused inputs expect the host's exact 400 text, or its prefix or a fragment where the text carries a value: a seed of k - 1 bases, an N at position 50 (the position named), a random 100 bp seed absent from the graph (on a single-graph server the whole request is a 400 whose text gives the seed's graph runs, SPEC-labeled-traversal-core section 6.1 step 2), graph and graphs on a single-graph server, a body that is not an object, 5 seeds against the server's `max_seeds` of 4, an unknown strategy key and an unknown bounds key (each named), `max_label_branches` 65 above its range of 0 to 64, an empty label list (named, with the way out: omit the field), an unknown label (named), `tip_window_bp` 5 (not implemented, section 6.5) and no seed. Accepted inputs expect a 200: two identical seeds, traversed again with the second result marked duplicate (section 6.1 step 6, `answer_fields`), and a budget of 70,000 ms lowered to the server's `max_time_ms` of 60,000 and stated in `strategy.clamped` (`clamped`, section 10.3). The expectation column is the host's; via MCP the family is decided by the service in the ways the table states per row, with the service's status and code (the counts here come from the same classifier as the cells): not expressible through MCP ({n_mcp_not_expressible} input{n_mcp_not_expressible:s}, no call made: {mcp_not_expressible_variants}); refused before host execution ({n_mcp_refused_before_host}: {mcp_refused_before_host_variants}); the host's refusal relayed through the service under its own code ({n_mcp_relayed}: {mcp_relayed_variants}); answered after service normalisation ({n_mcp_normalised}: {mcp_normalised_variants}); and answered by the host through the service ({n_mcp_answered}: {mcp_answered_variants}). The service merges identical seeds onto the first before sending, so via MCP the host answers one result where the direct request gets two, and more seeds than the host's `max_seeds` are sent in batches; the table explains both. [[n_mcp_by_design ? The {n_mcp_by_design} pair{n_mcp_by_design:s} standing by design are cases appendix B names[[mcp_by_design_all_verified ?, every one verified by the comparison | ({n_mcp_by_design_verified} verified, {n_mcp_by_design_unverified} not)]].]] The {n_mcp_not_exercised} not exercised have no MCP answer to compare.
T-edge.claim: every refusal carries the host's exact text, duplicate seeds are walked and marked, and a budget above the cap is lowered and stated

T-seeds.title: several seeds
T-seeds.prose: Three distinct 60 bp seeds of bsu, hvo and sso in one request, right traversal arm (direction), radius 200 bp: the answer holds one result per seed in the request's order, each walked under its own labels and budgets (SPEC-labeled-traversal-core section 5, the per-seed scopes), and each result's walk follows its own record (`walk_in_record` with the seed's index, record scope). [[manifest_version = 5 ? And a seed of mpn's window under two labels, its header and the taxid column of an unrelated kingdom (mja), which lacks one of the window's k-mers (as R-multi's `label_not_full` assumes), with a client `seed_id`: the unrelated label is dropped as `seed_unsupported`, `labels_supporting_total` is 1, the id is echoed with `seed_id_mismatch` true (section 6.1 step 3), and the walk follows the record.]] In this run [[n_footnoted ? {n_footnoted:word} test{n_footnoted:s} [[n_footnoted = 1 ? carries | carry]] a detail block (an access path did not pass, or the paths answered differently): {footnoted_ids}; the exception index on the chapter page says what each exception means, the block holds the record | every test passed on every access path exercised, with the paths' answers alike]].

T-graphlet.title: graphlet output
T-graphlet.prose: `output.detail` graphlet (SPEC-labeled-traversal-core section 7.5: per seed a JSON summary with the whole result as MGT v1 text, from which the SPEC says the full detail is reproduced) on a 60 bp seed of mtb and of mja under the record's header, radius 500 bp. The checks parse the MGT body into the full shape and read it as they read a full answer (the service's MCP export is a graphlet too), so the property is T-walk's: `walk_in_record` on the record's route and `traverse_seed_outcome` complete or partial. What this verifies is a serialisation-path witness: the body decodes, and the decoded result holds a route following the record with a complete or partial outcome. It does not compare the decoded result with a full-detail answer of the same seed (no such twin or relation is in this manifest), so the identity of every branch, label, coordinate and path between the two representations, the losslessness the SPEC asserts, is not verified here, and a body spelling another walk that still held the record's route would pass. T-quorum.title: label quorum

[[manifest_version = 5 ? The permit side: the same seed under its header and its taxid column, both carrying every k-mer of the record, so two labels stay live and the walk follows the record (`walk_in_record`, radius 200 bp).]] In this run [[n_footnoted ? {n_footnoted:word} test{n_footnoted:s} [[n_footnoted = 1 ? carries | carry]] a detail block (an access path did not pass, or the paths answered differently): {footnoted_ids}; the exception index on the chapter page says what each exception means, the block holds the record | every test passed on every access path exercised, with the paths' answers alike]].
T-quorum.claim: below the label quorum every path ends at once[[manifest_version = 5 ?; at the quorum the walk follows the record]]

T-strand.title: reverse-complement seed
T-strand.prose: The reverse complement of a 60 bp window of buc none of whose reverse k-mers buc holds (the window is chosen so), sent as a seed under buc's header, radius 100 bp. On this basic graph a k-mer and its reverse complement are different nodes and the index holds the records' forward strands, so the seed is refused (400) by one of the two seed refusals of SPEC-labeled-traversal-core section 6.1: not fully present in the graph when some reverse k-mer is in no record of the graph (step 2), no seed label supports every k-mer when other records hold them all (step 3); [[manifest_version = 5 ? which one the index gives is empirical (tag index-empirical: the first in v3 and v4), and the expectation is their common prefix naming the seed, so either passes | the expectation is the step-2 refusal's text, the seed named as not fully present in the graph with its graph runs, the refusal v3 and v4 observed on this index (v5 admits either, tagged index-empirical)]]. This is the traverse-side statement of the strand fact R-rc and chapter N test on their routes. [[x[T-strand-0001][mcp][class] = relayed ? Via MCP the host's refusal came back relayed under the service's own code, and the pair agrees.]] In this run [[n_footnoted ? the test carries a detail block (an access path did not pass, or the paths answered differently): {footnoted_ids}; the exception index on the chapter page says what the exception means | the refusal came on every access path exercised, the answers alike]].
T-strand.claim: a reverse-complement seed is refused on this forward-strand graph

T-walk.property: A walk from a seed of the record, constrained to the record's header or taxid column, spells the record's own continuation of the seed to the minimum the record sets (its first second successor, its first reused edge, its end, or the radius), or ends earlier at a stated branch or re-entry: one witness route per requested direction, not every route of the answer; `outcome.walks` complete or partial.
T-walk.note: The groups vary the direction and the radius; the seeds (31 to 200 bp) and the records vary with them: correctness controls across radii and records, not a runtime-versus-radius benchmark (latency varies substantially across seeds and records; these controls do not isolate the effect of the radius).
T-walk.question: Does a walk constrained to the record's header or taxid column follow the record's own continuation of the seed to the minimum the record sets (one witness route per direction), or end earlier at a stated branch?

T-longwalk.property: The gate's walk of a seed (500, 1,000 or 5,000 bp under 60,000 ms, constrained to the record's taxid column) and its long twin, the same seed walked 10,000 bp under the same budget (budget_stress, outside the deploy gate): each follows the record to the record's minimum or ends at a stated branch, and a stop by the budget is stated and possible (then inconclusive, never a pass).
T-longwalk.question: Do the gate's column walks and their 10,000 bp long twins follow the record under 60,000 ms, or end at a stated branch, with any budget stop stated and possible?

T-derived.property: A seed without explicit labels (permit per_hit): the host derives the carrier set, the labels supporting every seed k-mer, and a route of each traversal arm (direction) follows the record (1,000 bp, or a stated branch or re-entry earlier); the result is complete or partial, never failed.
T-derived.question: Does a seed sent without labels walk under the carrier set the host derives, a route following the record?

T-end.property: A 31 bp seed 40 to 100 bp from a record end, walked toward it under the record's header: the route following the record ends exactly at the record's end, with reason `label_lost` or `dead_end`.
T-end.question: Does a walk toward a record's end stop exactly at the end, with reason `label_lost` or `dead_end`?

T-repeat.property: A seed inside a multi-copy repeat, walked [[manifest_version = 5 ? 400 | 1,000]] bp both ways under the record's header: a split or branch event at or before the depth where the record's copies diverge, and a route follows one of the copies for its minimum.
T-repeat.question: Inside a multi-copy repeat, does the walk state a branch where the record's copies diverge, and does a route follow one copy?

T-labels.property: annotate mode lists every structural successor and a route follows the record; a derived set of the kind asked (column or header) holds the record's own label and no label of another kind; `max_labels_per_node` 1 is echoed per traversal arm, the walk unchanged (a cut list, which a single header label cannot produce, is not exercised).
T-labels.question: Does annotate mode follow every structural successor, does a derived set hold the record's own label of the kind asked, and is `max_labels_per_node` echoed?

T-exhaustive.property: The exhaustive trie (the trie preset, radius 100 bp) under the record's header: a leaf follows the record to its minimum.
T-exhaustive.question: Does the exhaustive trie hold the record's own walk as a leaf (a witness leaf; the trie's completeness is the server's certificate)?

T-coords.property: trace support with `output.coordinates` under the record's header: the seed's occurrence is [start, start + length) in the record and each traversal arm's run from the seed boundary lies adjacent to it (positions in the record's bases, not k-mer starts); the walk follows the record.
T-coords.question: With trace support, are the reported coordinates the record's: the seed's occurrence at its place and each direction's run adjacent to it?

T-budget.property: Each bound set alone (`time_budget_ms` 1, `max_memory_mb` 1, `max_work_units` 300,000, `max_steps` 5) stops the walk with its own stated reason (a `resource_stop` of time, memory or work with the request's value; a cap trigger for `max_steps`), a limitation names the knob, and the walk so far follows the record.
T-budget.question: Does each bound set alone stop the walk with its own stated reason and knob, the walk so far following the record (a stated stop, not a latency bound)?

T-attempts.property: The attempt lifecycle: a `not_after_ms` in the past is 409 expired before any work; an `attempt_id` answers 200 with `usage` and the bound the server enforces (seeds 1, the preset's 15,000 ms, the allowance of 10,000 ms, `walk_until_ms`); the same id sent again while retained is 409 duplicate, carrying the attempt's state and usage[[manifest_version = 5 ? | (the second repeat of T-attempts-0002: allowed, its 200-only checks inconclusive)]].
T-attempts.question: Is an expired request refused before any work, does an attempt state its usage and bound, and is a retained id refused as a duplicate?

T-edge.property: Malformed seeds, unknown keys and out-of-range knobs are refused with 400 and the host's exact text (or prefix); duplicate seeds are walked again and marked; a budget above the server's cap is lowered and stated in `strategy.clamped`. The expectation is the host's; the MCP cell says how the service answered.
T-edge.question: Is a malformed request refused with the host's exact text, are duplicate seeds walked and marked, and is a budget above the cap lowered and stated?

T-seeds.property: Three seeds of three records in one request: each result's walk follows its own record.[[manifest_version = 5 ? A seed of two labels one of which does not support it: that label dropped `seed_unsupported`, one left, the client's `seed_id` echoed with its mismatch stated, the walk in the record.]]
T-seeds.question: Is each seed of one request walked under its own labels, each result's walk following its own record?

T-graphlet.property: `output.detail` graphlet: the MGT body (with its JSON summary) decodes to a result in which a route follows the record and the outcome is complete or partial, as in a full answer; the equivalence with a full-detail answer of the same seed is not compared.
T-graphlet.question: Does the graphlet body decode to a result holding the record's route with a complete or partial outcome?

T-caps.property: A cap per traversal arm, that is, direction (`max_output_bp` 50[[manifest_version = 5 ?; the trie's `max_live_paths` 2 and `max_paths` 1]]) truncates the direction it trips on, names itself in `cap_trigger` and a limitation, and the walk so far is in the record[[manifest_version = 5 ?; `max_live_paths` above the service's maximum is walked by the host and refused by the service by design]].
T-caps.question: Does a cap per traversal arm truncate the direction it trips on, name itself, and leave the walk so far in the record?

T-quorum.property: `min_live_labels` 2 on a seed of one header label: every path ends `below_min_labels` at once, at most 1 bp (SPEC section 6.4)[[manifest_version = 5 ?; on a seed of its header and its taxid column, both carrying every record k-mer, the walk follows the record]].
T-quorum.question: Below the label quorum, does every path end at once?

T-strand.property: The reverse complement of a record window none of whose reverse k-mers the record holds, as a seed under the record's header: refused by one of the two seed refusals of SPEC section 6.1 (not fully present in the graph; no seed label supports every k-mer), whichever the index gives.
T-strand.question: Is a reverse-complement seed refused on this forward-strand graph by one of the two seed refusals?

units.T-coords: Not exercised via MCP: `traverse_fetch` cannot set `output.coordinates` (an override outside bounds, direction, exhaustive and the two label knobs), although the trace preset itself is accepted; see B.
units.T-attempts: Not exercised via MCP: the attempt fields (`attempt_id`, `not_after_ms` and the others) are the service's own, sent by its worker, and the caller cannot set them; see B.

purpose: /traverse answers the second question a user asks: given a piece of sequence the index knows (a seed), how does the indexed sequence continue beyond it, and under which labels? It extends the seed base by base through the graph in one or both directions, following only successors some permitted label supports, and returns the routes it found with a stated reason for every end. Where /resolve checks support for a supplied sequence, /traverse builds new sequence from a supplied seed. This chapter's evidence is of the second kind of I.2's ground truth, a witness: for each walk the builder knows one correct continuation, the source record's own, and the check asks that some returned route spells it to a minimum computed from the record; it does not enumerate every route the graph admits, and a route the walker follows under a taxid column is supported step by step by some record of the taxon, not necessarily one record throughout (label support, I.1; the Background says what a pass proves). The evidence map after the headline lists each family's claim and what the direct access paths showed of it; the exception index and the detail blocks hold the exceptions.
